item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Ahrweiler, Germany on January 30, 1919

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
USA

Ahrweiler, Germany
30 Jan 1919
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received letter from Papa today dated Jan 10th. Doesn’t take mail very long to get here now. Certainly was glad to get it. Glad to know Ruby has recovered from the flu. First I had heard of her sickness. Sure is good to know you are all well. I’m still on the same job but expect to attend school at Coblens commencing next Monday. Cobblers is a pretty large city. Not much news about when we will leave but general impression is that we will start about the 1st of March. Certainly hope we do cause I’m mighty anxious to get home. Picked up some Radio press last night. Said 42nd and 32nd divisions would be first complete national guard units home and 77th Division would be first drafted division home. Like to get home and bid in some of there jobs that are on bulletin.
Having a show here nearly every night. Will mail you some of the programs if I can find them. Having a German grand opera tonight but I’m on duty and can’t go. However they’re having another one tomorrow night so guess I’ll go to it. Doesn’t cost anything. Have a swell theatre, looks just like the ones in the states.
Forgot to mention that I received letter from Papa other day enclosing copy of Mr. Doocy’s letter. Glad you mailed them a copy of my letter. If I’m ever in Pittsfield I’ll call on them.
Found out about my allotment today. it’s still infect and will continue until I get out of the army.
Hope you’re getting it regularly. I’ve been feeling just fine. Feel like I want to get out and run all the time. Have a great big feather bed to sleep in. Get lots of sleep, plenty to eat and not much work. I’ll be all ready to go to work after I see you all and visit Ruby and Grace.
Think we get one months extra pay when we’re discharged. That will by me a suit of clothes. It wont take me long to make enough to fit myself out with plenty of clothing. Certainly would like to get into a suit of civilian clothes again.
Rumor has it that when we leave here we sail on the Rhine up to Belgium. Sounds plausible.
Division is ranting 14 day leaves now to men who wish to visit relatives in Scotland, Ireland, England, or Italy. Guess that doesn’t include me case if I have any relatives in any of those countries I don’t know it. Besides I haven’t the funds to provide for such a trip. Wouldn’t mind going to Italy. They say Rome is a wonderful place. I’ll be satisfied if they’ll just send me home though. Don’t think I’ll ever cross the Atlantic again, once I get on the other side. Hows Knox making it? Certainly was tickled to hear about Audrey talking in her sleep and saying “God Bless her little heart.” Ha ha.
I certainly did get the Christmas box and I want to say that I enjoyed it ever so much. I’ve a lot of back mail coming yet if it ever gets here.
Be glad when the Conference gets a peace treaty ready for Germany to sing. Hope they get things settled in Russia. See where our troops are fighting there.

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: France on November 2, 1918

France Nov. 2nd ’18
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all,
Thought I’d write a few lines this pm while I had the stationary handy. Am still in hospital so have had no mail since last writing. Wont get any until I get back to my organization. I’m feeling fine and dandy and am up all the time during the day. Will be getting out before long. Notice in paper where Turkey has capitulated and it looks as though Austria will follow suit so that will leave Germany all alone. Looks as though the war was approaching the grand finale. I’d certainly love to see it over by Christmas. You’ve all read of the Lt. Mitice drive. Our division started that drive and went all the way through it besides holding the line for quite a while after it was over. Can’t mention anything about our work since that time. Noticed that in the paper so concluded ’twas permissible for me to mention it. The allies have been doing some tall scrapping, especially the Americans. They had the hardest piece of ground to take of any of them and they’re still scrapping.
Well its about supper time so must stop and peddle the coffee. I’m on K.P. here. ha. Hope you are all we’ll. Don’t worry any about me.
Lovingly,
Martin
Crp M. W. Chandler
Co “C” 117 FBSC – AEF

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: France on October 24, 1918

France Oct. 24th – 1918
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Haven’t written for so long that I guess you all will think I’ve quit writing altogether. This is first chance I’ve had to write for some time. Wrote you the 3rd of Oct. but had no chance to mail it. I’ve received lots letters from all of you since last writing. Have received two from Grace enclosing Kodaks of Audrey. They sure were dandy pictures especially the last one (the one taken when she was lying on the bed) I’ve been in hospital since the 18th. Am getting along OK and expect to be out soon. Got sick while at the front. Am enclosing a christmas pkg. coupon but don’t suppose it will reach you in time. If it doesn’t, don’t worry any about sending an xmas pkg.
have certainly had a nice time during past two months. Tell you all about it when we get home. Been quite a bit of peace talk floating around lately but I’m not very sanguine. How are the girls getting along in Wichita? Guess I’d better ask them though. Sure glad Margaret and Lucerne are attending school there instead of at home. See in the paper where the Liberty Loan went over the top by 150 million. That’s about what we all expected. People over there sure are keeping their end up.
Guess I wont get any more mail until I get back to the outfit. Don’t know when that will be. I’m feeling pretty good now except that I’m rather weak. Heard Ruby was expecting next month. Sure hope she comes through ok.
We’ve een having some very rainy weather over here for past month. Nothing unusual though. How’s Knox getting along with school? Who is his teacher?
This ought to get home just about Papa’s birthday so dad, here’s wishing you many happy returns of the day.
Am going to Answer Grace and Lorin’s letter soon as I get some stationary. In fact I’ll answer everybody’s letters and I’ll try and write you all real often while I have the chance.
The Allies have certainly been delivering some fearful wallops to the Huns. Kinda got ’em hollering for peace now.
Well must close. Hope this finds you all well. Don’t worry any about me.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martim Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed On: October 12, 1918

Oct. 12 1918
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all,
Didn’t geta chance to mail my letter of 3rd so will add few more lines. Received letter from papa other day and sure glad to get it. Papa keeps them coming pretty regularly. Haven’t much time to write but don’t know much to write anyway. Certainly been busy past month and lots to put up with. No one kicking through, nights are very cold now and have been having lots of rainy weather. Have travelled considerably since last writing. Mostly on foot.
Sure would like to see the Germans surrender so we could come home. The allies are giving them the dickens on all sides. Heard about German’s request for an armistice. Don’t think they will get any satisfaction until they pull their troops in.
I’ve been feeling fine and dandy. Hope you all are well.
I’ll answer Grace’s letter at first opportunity. Don’t know the girl’s address in Wichita. Bess didn’t mention it in her letter. I’ll have to close now. Going to try and rustle something to eat. Everybody write.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Little Silver, New Jersey on September 29th, 1918

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike County

Sept 29th
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received papa’s letter day before yesterday and another today and also received mama’s and Bess’ dandy letters enclosing Johns and Aunt Anna’s and I certainly enjoyed them all. Was mighty glad to get them. Was first mail I’ve received since leaving Ft. Bliss. Am over at club tonight. Was at YMCA Thursday and Friday nights. Had a social Thursday night. In fact they have on every Thursday. Good program. Served ice cream and cake. Friday night was formal opening and dedication of YMCA. Had good speaking and good program. Enjoyed it very much. These sure are good places to pass away time at night. All kinds of amusements. Lots of good books, both at YMCA and Club. The people here are very hospitable and some notable financial powers live in immediate vicinity of this place. Wilsons son-in-law lives only four miles from here. Was glad to get Lesley Wildt’s address. Have been wanting it for past year. He and I used to chum together quite a bit. Haven’t located Lake Denmark yet but will do so tomorrow and if not very far will get to see him. It is now rumored that we sail about the 3rd of next month. But have heard nothing definite but think we will leave pretty soon. Just found out yesterday that I can have all or part of my pay sent home by government so I’ll put in a $20.00 allotment to be sent home each month. Had to give name of some relative today who should be notified in case of my death or an accident. All preparations indicate we will leave shortly. They’re not fixing up camp very much and wont build anything or order any stoves for us, and it’s pretty cold here too, so i guess we will leave shortly. I have another horse now. It’s a fine big black horse. Awful powerful and can run like the wind. It’s a great pet too. Did you get the Battalion picture ok? You didn’t mention it but suppose you did. I’ll try and have my picture taken with horse before I leave and send to you. Awful glad the children are getting along OK in school and mighty glad Lucerne can play so well. Wish I could have been there when Sam and all the rest were at home. I’d like mighty welt see Audrey Grace. To think I’ve a close relative that I can’t see and don’t when when I can – I’ll bet she is a cute kid. We had General Inspecting this morning. Had all out filled equipment laid out and cleaned up nicely. Also had pistol inspection. We all have 45 Caliber Colts automatics. Sure are good guns. Thats all the weapons we have. Don’t stand much show if we should happen to be compelled to repair or construct line of communication under fire. Of course we wont fight any this winter. Will probably train all winter in France and be ready for spring. Lots of men leaving everyday now for France. Uncle Sam is gathering them over there pretty fast.
Golly I’ll certainly appreciate the sweater the girls are knitting. It will come in mighty handy. Yes, mama I’ve heard the songs you mentioned. “Over There” and “America Here’s my Boy.” Thats about all they sing out here. They all like “Over There” best of all. Glad to hear Aunt Sarah received her back pension money. Sure hope she stays well and is feeling good. Golly papa I’d like o be there and help out with the work. I know what apple season is there. All the crops through Missouri and Kansas are best ever so the farmers said when we passed through there. Is Grimaly working at “Dr.” Papa? Sure hope you learn to use that bug OK cause its a great labor saver and you can do so much better with it after learning to use it. What branch of service is Wade Maynard in? Guess there will be quite a few go over before the war is over. Saw in paper yesterday where the Pope’s peace proposal had failed and he predicts the war will last for 3 years yet. Gee everything is high out here. Bacon is 47 cents pound. Eggs 70 cents dozen. Our laundry in Fr. Bliss cost each man $1.75 per month. No matter how much or how little we sen but I sent min in to Long Branch other day and it cost me $1.59 so it will amount to quite a little in a month. Well must close . Everybody write often. If can do so will give you address soon as we get across.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: France on May 13, 1918

E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
USA

France May 13th 1918
Dearest Papa, Mama, & all,
Wrote you several days ago but it came back yesterday account containing too much news. Ha. Also one sent back which I had to Ruby so now I’ll have to do them over. I received 2 letters from Papa yesterday. One dated in Feb forwarded from other company and one dated in April. That makes 7 letters I’ve received from you all in lat 3 days. Sure was mighty glad to get them. Ruby, Grace, Lorin, and Bess all wrote dandy long letters. Very much surprised to hear of Grover’s marriage. Hope they get along OK. Bess told me of Lee Maynard’s marriage also. Lots of the fellows under 31 getting married since last June. Ha.
Guess I can’t tell you much news. My last effort was a failure have quite a bit of time tonight so guess I’ll write everybody a letter. Ruby, Grace, and Bess. Has Bess gone to Wichita yet? Ruby said she was coming. Well I finally received my service record and will get my 6 months pay this pay day. It will be $20.00 shy account of an allotment that you all didn’t get and therefore due me. You remember I told you last Jan that when I changed the allotment last November it cancelled the former one and the 20.00 for Nov. wasn’t sent home and on the Jan pay roll it was marked due me but wasn’t on the pay role this month. Guess I’ll get it next month. I can use the frances very nicely. Am out of Soviet articles. Are you getting the allotment regularly? Glad you got the insurance policy. I never have received any of the packages you mentioned having sent. Don’t have the last idea where they are. Hope papa gets that raise to 12. That wont be so bad.
Were having dandy weather except for rain. Everybody has their garden in. We still draw rations and do our own cooking. Like it fine. Guess you all feel the effects of the war. Relative foodstuffs, etc. I see by the “Communique” from Paris that the 3rd Liberty loan was a grand success.
The YMCAs are going great work over here. Furnish all sorts of entertainment. There were two American girls sang at YMCA here last week. Sure was a sight for sore eyes. I notice they kept gazing at a shell hole in the roof and were rather startled every time on of our “berthas” sent over a kiss to the Kaiser. Ha.
Well I must close and get busy on the rest of the letters. Don’t pass this one around cause I’m going to write them all one just like it. Ha.
Am feeling great and getting along OK. Don’t worry about me. Will write again, soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: France on April 30th, 1918

Pvt. M. W. Chandler
Co “C” 117 F.B.S.C
42nd Division=A.E.F.

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
USA

France April 30th, 1918
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received Mama’s dandy long letter yesterday dated April 1st and mighty glad to get it. Wish you would keep them coming. I haven’t received my serve record yet consequently no pay and don’t have the slightest idea when I will.
Certainly is disgusting to hear about the Pro Germans around there. They should be put in jail as German sympathizers. I wish some Govt. official would hear Heddler make a remark like “Dog collars should be put on all soldiers and called Wilson’s pups.” That’s German sympathy pure and simple. I wish some of them could come in contact with these Germans. I consider it great sport to elevate a big fat german on the end of a Bayonet and hear him squeal. They’re just like their government – greedy and inhuman. I’ll surely be glad when they are cleaned up which, of course, will be the eventual outcome of this war.
Nothing new to write. Getting along OK and feeling fine. If you can secure copy of Kansas City post of Mar. 14th you will see some interesting news. Grinsley might get you a copy. Hope Bill gets in good branch of service if he is selected. Wish I could have been there when the sausage arrived. Ha.
Hope you have good luck with your garden down by Quarry.
We’ve been having lots rain over here. Wish it would dry up. Well I must stop, all of you write and don’t worry about me. I’ll write as often as I can.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Ahrwieler, Germany on March 19th, 1918

Dearest Papa, Mama, and all,
Received latter from Papa yesterday and was mighty glad to get it. Pretty near every mail brings in a letter from Papa. Well, theres new dope out now that we wont leave for some time. They got orders not to turn over equipment until further notice. Darn it! Seems like something comes up every time to change things. Will enclose the speech delivered us by Gen. Pershing up on Rhine last Sunday. Sure was a dandy review. Everything went lovely.
Been having some rain and snow lately but today is pretty day.
Heard rumor that we will go through France and not up the Rhine. Certainly hope it isn’t true. Sure would hate to go through France. probably have to lay in France for couple of weeks if we go through there.
We don’t belong to the 4th Army Corps any more. Are now 3rd Army reserve. Certainly hope we start for home soon cause I’m mighty anxious to get there. I’ll be sure and fill out the blank you received from Pittsfield. Are they just for men from Pike County?
Well, haven’t much time to write this and don’t know much more to write. So will close. Hope you are all well
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Ahrweiler, Germany on January 13, 1918

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
USA

Ahrweiler, Germany
Jan 13th, 1918
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all,
No mail since last writing. Expecting to receive my back mail most any day. Sure be glad when it comes. Nothing new to write about. Still having mild weather.
Am working in Message Center here. Recording correspondence, telegrams, etc. Doesn’t require much clerical ability. Work from 8 am to 5 pm and in addition, work half night every fourth night. Don’t have much to do at night but keep pretty busy during the day. have a good warm place to sleep. Getting good meals here. Have been feeling extremely good past month.
Notice in paper when they are busting men out of service, at a rapid rate in the states. Will certainly be glad when we get back. Don’t have the least idea when that will be. Hear lots of rumors but, of course, one can’t believe them. The A.E.F. has got an Old Maids sewing circle backed clear of the map when it comes to starting rumors.
Was much surprised to hear of Colonel Roosevelt’s death. The Country will sure miss him.
Our signal Corps Radio picks up the states, Russia, Honolulu and many other places. Get lots of press from the states.
The German people treat us very good. Do almost anything for a fellow. Guess they’re depending a great deal on the U.S. helping them out in the future.
Well must close for this time. Hope you are all well. Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: New Jersey on December 17, 1917

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike County

Dec 16th, ’17
Dearest Folks,
Have received 2 letters from Papa since last writing. Guess you’ll think I’ve quit writing altogether. I’ve written twice. But as usual didn’t mail them. They weren’t very long letters anyway. Just a note.
Have been working like the dickens past week. It has snowed every day. Now 8:30 pm and we just got through loading our combat wagons, trucks, motorcycles, and other boxes and will load the horses tomorrow and leave Tuesday for sure so you needn’t write me anymore until you hear from me again. Needn’t mention to anyone that we have gone.
Will write you as often as possible from over there but don’t expect any descriptions of country, etc cause it isn’t allowed.
Got letter from Chas Morgan at St. Louis other day. It was in the dead letter office for some time account he didn’t put my organization on envelope. Will enclose it. Today is Knox’s birthday. Wish I had something to send. I’m broke cause didn’t draw any pay this month.
I haven’t read the insurance policy yet. Guess they will mail it direct to you. I changed my mind and made it for $10,000.00 in case I did you will get about $58.00 per month for 20 years and in case of death of beneficiary it goes to next closest relative and sundown until it is all paid. Again if I should be disabled I would receive a pretty nice income. It goes $6.50 per month on $10,000.00. That will leave me about 3.00 per month which I think will be all I’ll need. Did you ever hear in regard to increase on my allotment? Sure hope you get it.
I’m feeling fine and have plenty of warm clothing and will make it OK so don’t worry about me. We have a dandy Captain. He is always looking out for our health and comfort.
Well I’ll stop and turn in cause I’m sure tired.
Here’s wishing everybody a merry merry Christmas and Happy New Years and hope I’ll be with you on the next Xmas.
Knox here’s best wishes for a happy birthday and hope I’ll see a big strapping fellow when I get back.
Will let you hear from me soon as can.
Lots love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Margaret Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Margaret Chandler
Mailed From: Little Silver, New Jersey on November 2, 1917

Miss Margaret Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike County

Nov 2nd, 1917
Dearest Margaret,
Received your letter some time ago and sure glad to get it. Wish you’d write often. Hows school coming? Guess you’re having a great time playing basket ball. Gee it will soon be Christmas. Seems an age since I’ve spent an Xmas at home. Sure hope I’ll be at home some Christmas. Don’t know where I’ll be this Christmas. Kinda looks as thought we were going to leave before soon. But can’t tell much about it. Didn’t expect to be here now.
Sure is cold here. Having lots rain too. Makes it awful disagreeable. I’m sure having a peach of a time in the kitchen. Lots of work to do. Get up at 5:30 am and work until 6:30 pm. Wash dishes, pans, peel spuds, onions, and do a little bit of everything. Carry coal and cut wood each day. I’ll be off tomorrow night and I’ll sure be glad of it.
Wrote Bess last night and put a 2 cent stamp on it so guess she will have to pay a penny to get it out. Didn’t think about having to put 3 cent on it.
When are you going to Morrisonville? How is Audrey? Golly Id sure love to see her and the rest of you all.
Well I don’t know anything to write tonight so will stop.
Be sure and write as often as you can cause I sure love to get the letters.
Hope everybody is well.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Camp Alfred Vail, Litte Silver, New Jersey on October 8, 1917

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike County

M.W. Chandler
Co B 1st FBSC
Little Silver, NJ

Camp Alfred Vail
Little Silver, NJ 9th 1917
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received 3 letters from papa since last writing and mighty glad to get them. Was so sorry to hear Knox has broken his arm and I’ll be anxious to hear when he is OK again. That will keep him out of school too. Be sure and let me know how he gets along. Nothing much new to write except were all afraid we wont get to go to France for awhile. We’re all prepared to leave but nobody know anything about when we are going. Some think the company will be split up and sent to different places as non commissioned officers to drill the National army. Everybody thought we would leave immediately and its sure some disappointment to think we might not go. Can’t tell anything about it though.
I’m on guard duty now. On at 5:30 pm yesterday and off at 5:30 this pm. Do guard duty 2 hours off four hours. It’s pretty cold here at nights but have good warm clothing and a dandy overcoat. I’ll sure be glad to get that sweater. Overcoats are so unhandy to go out to drill but got to wear something to keep warm and that sweater will make it fine and dandy.
I just got away from the guard house for few mins to come over to YMCA and write. Hands are so cold can hardly write.
I’ll be over at club tomorrow night and will write from there.
Be sure and let me know how Knox makes it. Hope rest of you are all well.
In case we leave unexpectedly will write you if permitted.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Little Silver, New Jersey on September 28, 1917

M.W. Chandler
Co “B” 1st Field Battalion
Camp Alfred Vail
Little Silver, N.J.

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill.
Pike County

Camp Alfred, Vail 26th
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Golly Havent received any mail since being here. Thought sure would have received a letter before now. Everything going along OK. Awful chilly here but otherwise like it OK. Haven’t heard anything definite as to when we will go to France but were sure going. I’m anxious to get over there. 25 Signal Corps men and 3 officers left today for Franc. 2 come over to the Signal Corps Club nearly every night. Good way to pass time away. Have a dandy Victrola and piano. All kinds books and magazines to read. Been doing lot of fatigue since coming here getting camp straightened out. I haven’t been on a horse since leaving Texas but will go out tomorrow on drill. How are the children coming in school? Is the apple season over yet papa? How much does Grace’s baby weigh now? Lordy I’d love to see her. Did she enter the contest at the state fair? Well guess I’ll go down and finish my story. Am reading “The Dark Star” by Chambers. Have to be back in camp by 11 pm. We all drew overcoats yesterday. The sure are dandy. Will get rest of our winter clothing right away. Fitzjarrellz is over here with me tonight. You know he is the fellow I mentioned from White Hall. Does Ruby remember him? He used to go with Lucille Knox.
Well must stop. Hurry up and write.
Love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Fort Bliss, Texas on August 27, 1917

M.W. Chandler
Co “B” 1st F.B.S.C.
Ft. Bliss

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
Pike County

Co “B” 1st FBSC
Ft. Bliss Texas
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received 2 letters from papa since returning from hike last Saturday evening and sure glad to get them. We went up into New Mexico on the hike. Had a dandy time. The company was split up and strung out through the country and we had continuos wire communication which we put up ourselves. I stayed on duty until midnight. A and C company were along too. A company is the Radio outfit. They put up their wireless apparatus and were in communication with El Paso all the time. They also had a wire strung to our camp and out company relayed all messages for El Paso to the Radio Co and they sent them by wireless to El Paso and Ft. Bliss.
The man who brought Papa’s letter to me yesterday saw that it was from Pearl and asked me if I knew anyone there. I told him I lived there and he said he was from White Hall. He sleeps in tent next to mine. He is a step brother of Pearl Ellis and said he remembered Ruby and Pearl were at their house one time. His name is Fitzjarrellz. He is Corporal in the company and a nice fellow. He also knows Uncle Will’s family at Manchester and used to go with Lucille. Sure surprised me to meet him. Said he had been at Pearl lots of times playing ball and coming to boat shows and knows lots of the fellows around Pearl. He’s the only fellow I’ve ran across close from home. Our battalion played baseball with 2nd telegraph battalion yesterday and beat them 7 to 3. Captain was sure pleased. I had m picture taken in ball suit with another fellow. Just a Kodak. Will send you one soon as they are finished. Mama did you ever find the Kodaks in my suit case?
Well its just 5 min until drill time and I’ve been writing this in an awful hurry so could get it off this am.
Hope everybody is OK. Well write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed On: July 31, 1917

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ills
Pike Co

July 31st
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received letter from papa day before yesterday and one today and mighty glad to get them. General Representative of Russia was here today reviewing our troops. They had a big parade, about 12000 soldiers. Gee it sure looked pretty. As far back as I could see was column after column of soldiers. The signal corps was up toward the front, mounted. I had a pretty good house. By golly from the way paper reads the general had better beat it to Russia. Haven’t heard anything about how long will be here but couldn’t be surprised if didn’t stay here until next spring. It’s pretty warm here in day time but the night are always cool and have to cover up. Thane good thing. Awful glad the girls got their pass to Dunlap. I’ll write to them tonight in this company from Illinois. Sure seems good to see dome one from up there. What is Ralph doing? Hope he gets a job OK. I saw in paper where all the switches around Chad were on a strike. Hope it doesn’t delay the girls trip any.
Well I’m in a hurry. Got to get ready to stand retreat. Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Santa Margarita, CA on September 18, 1916

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
Pike Co

Santa Margarita Sept 18th
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received Mama’s letter yesterday and haven’t heard from papa in a coons age. Sure was glad to get Mama’s letter. This is first time I’ve written for several days. Getting along OK and will be on this job at least a month longer and probably 2 months. Agent has gone to New York so regular 3rd trick man got his job leaving me here for while longer. Sure have a bunch of train orders to handle. Keeps me going sometimes. Getting pretty cool out there at night. Have to have a fire every night. See in the paper where they have rented the M.E. Church for Primary room. Thought they had built a new school house there or had added to the old one. See they’ve started on the ditch again. I’d like to see it.
I’ve been going up to the school-man’s house nearly every night. We all went swimming other day. Gee they have swell schoolhouse here. Have piano, dance floor, opera house, and everything in it. Have some pretty swell scenery on the stage. It’s a single story building but has 4 rooms besides the opera and dance room. Sure is swell.
Gee I sure was tickled when agent told me he was going to lay off 2 months. Felt pretty sure I’d get to stay on this job. Ruby is making a pretty good visit at Grace’s. Wish I was there.
Well I must stop and get busy. Bell rings just about every 10 or 15 min for 9.00. Wish you’d all write a little more often.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: France on March 10

France Mar 10th
Dearest Folks,
Will write just few lines tonight while have good chance. Nothing new to write. Have received no mail yet. Suppose it will be several months before you can get a letter to me at this address. Requires quite a while to get an answer to a letter.
Have moved since last writing. Would like to tell you of our locations. Things are pretty warm here.
Been having some very nice weather here for past week. Hope it continues.
I’ve been feeling very good. Get plenty to eat. Have a pretty good YMCA here. Affords a good place to write letters.
Well must close and turn in. Am on K.P. now and have to get up at 4 am.
Hope you are all feeling well.
Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin
P.S. Dont have any of my letters put in “Tribune.”

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: France on February 28

Dearest Folks,
Have been traveling about quite a bit since last writing you. Was transferred to the 117th F.B.S.C. Feb 12. Like the organization very well and if I had my mail, clothes, etc from the 1st FB would just as soon stay with this organization. My service record is still with my old company. Don’t know when I’ll get a pay. Haven’t received any pay since October. Would like very much to get the mail you’ve already sent to me at 1st FB. But don’t know whether or not it will be forwarded here.
Been having some very rainy weather the past week. Guess this is the rainy season. First I’ve seen since being over here.
Would like to tell you of our whereabouts but of course that’s forbidden.
Am feeling very good. Only hope you are all feeling as well. Must stop for this time. Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin
Address: Pvt. Martin W. Chandler
Co ‘C” 117 F.B.D.C.
A.E.F.
Via New York

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: France on January 27

France Jan 27
Dearest Folks,
Intended writing yesterday but out it off until today.
Will leave hospital tomorrow but probably wont join my company for a month. Will go from here to convalescent camp and will be there 2 weeks and then go to base where will remain while longer so guess I wont get any mail for some time yet as all my mail will be with company.
